title: Non-inferiority of videolaryngoscopy-assisted intubation without neuromuscular blockade versus with neuromuscular blockade on first-attempt intubation success: a randomized clinical trial
official: VISION - Non-Inferiority of videolaryngoscopy-assisted intubation without neuromuscular blockade versus with neuromuscular blockade on first-attempt intubation success free of major complications: a randomized clinical trial
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to demonstrate the non-inferiority of VL-guided tracheal intubation without NMBA (VL/placebo) compared to VL-guided intubation with NMBA (atracurium) (VL/atracurium) in achieving successful tracheal intubation on the first attempt.
conditions: Adult patients requiring elective general anaesthesia with tracheal intubation for a surgical procedure requiring a neuromuscular blocking agent to ease the surgery.

interventions.name: ATRACURIUM HIKMA 10 mg/mL, solution injectable/pour perfusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. -	Adult patient aged 18 and over,
2. -	Scheduled for a procedure requiring general anaesthesia with tracheal intubation,
3. -	Surgical procedure requiring a neuromuscular blocking agent to ease the surgery
Exclusion criteria:
1. -	Any risk factors for pulmonary aspiration (such as absence of fasting, gastroparesis, hiatal hernia, gastroesophageal reflux disease),
2. -	Difficult or impossible intubation planned: o	Anatomical factors: Mallampati score III or IV, limited mouth opening (< 35 mm), short chin-to-neck distance (< 6 cm), limited neck mobility, high-arched or narrow plate, retrognathia, elevated neck circumference (> 45,6 cm), o	Clinical history and patient factors: previous difficult intubation, obstructive sleep apnoea or STOP-BANG score ≥ 5, head and neck radiation or surgery, craniofacial abnormalities, tracheal stenosis, morbid obesity (body mass index > 30 kg.m-2), pre-eclampsia, o	Emergency situations: ear-nose-throat pathology, cervico-facial trauma, facial or neck burns.
3. -	Patients with contraindication to neuromuscular blocking agents
4. -	Neuromuscular disease,
5. -	History of malignant hyperthermia
6. -	History of prolonged neuromuscular blockade,
7. -	Preoperative respiratory distress (SpO2 < 95% in ambient air),
8. -	Patients requiring specific induction protocols, such as rapid sequence induction using short-acting NMBAs
9. -	Suspected and unexplored history of hypersensitivity to neuromuscular blocking agents
10. -	Documented allergy to atracurium, cisatracurium, or benzenesulphonic acid
11. -	Clinically significant cardiovascular disease or any condition predisposing to unusual sensitivity to a fall in arterial blood pressure
12. -	Preoperative shock (Mean Arterial Pressure ≤ 65 mmHg or under vasopressor),
13. -	A procedure requiring intubation of a double-lumen endotracheal tube
14. -	Legal protection measures,
15. -	Absence of signed informed consent,
16. -	Simultaneous participation in another interventional clinical trial on a medicinal product or in another interventional clinical trial on intubation
17. -	Absence of affiliation to a social security regime.
18. -	Pregnancy and breast feeding,
19. -	Obesity, defined as body mass index over 30 kg.m-2,
